title: EDF preemptive surge log — louise
body:
Context:
Quick personal scratchpad to record EDF (earliest-deadline-first) preemption experiments against the synthetic surge generator 'tsurge'. Goal: understand whether lightweight EDF preemption at the request-queue level reduces p99 without blowing up overall throughput or increasing p50 too much for normal traffic.

Environment:
- Model: open-llama-13b-8k (quantized q4f) — representative of medium-large transformer in our hosted fleet
- Runtime: serving-runtime-dev branch (cuda-kernel-opt-2024-09) on A100-80GB
- Node config: 1 GPU per replica, 16 vCPU, 64GB RAM
- Workload generator: tsurge v0.9 (adds deadlines to requests, configurable burst shape)
- Arrival patterns: baseline Poisson (lambda set to steady qps), spike events modeled as Erlang-k clusters, and a long-tail heavy set (Pareto arrivals)
- Queue policy variants tested: FIFO (baseline), FIFO+soft-priority (background/foreground lanes), EDF-preemptive (single queue, preemption allowed with deadline checks), EDF-cohort (deadline buckets, no preempt but reordering)
- Measurement window: 20m warmup + 1h steady + 10m cooldown

Run summary (selected):
1) Baseline FIFO (steady 200 qps, spike to 800 qps for 30s every 2m)
- p50: 38 ms
- p95: 220 ms
- p99: 540 ms
- max throughput sustained in spike: 820 qps (some tail drops due to OOM backpressure)
- observations: long tail during spikes, occasional scheduler pauses when KV cache misses spike

2) FIFO + soft-priority lanes (foreground: 60% tokens, background: 40%, preemption is cooperative)
- p50 (foreground): 42 ms
- p95 (foreground): 180 ms
- p99 (foreground): 360 ms
- p50 (background): 120 ms
- note: improved foreground p99 vs baseline but background suffers; total successful requests slightly lower due to background starvation

3) EDF-preemptive (preempt at scheduling boundary, checkpoint lightweight KV state)
- p50: 55 ms
- p95: 130 ms
- p99: 180 ms
- observed throughput: stable ~800 qps during spikes, fewer tail spikes above 300ms
- CPU overhead: +8% scheduler cycles, GPU utilization slightly down (~4%) due to increased context switches
- anomalies: occasional failed preempt rollback when KV window >4k tokens -> request aborted (~0.02% of attempts)

4) EDF-cohort (deadline buckets of 50ms, 200ms, 500ms; no true preempt)
- p50: 48 ms
- p95: 150 ms
- p99: 260 ms
- throughput: comparable to FIFO+soft-priority; p99 better than FIFO but worse than preemptive EDF

Quick comparative table (human-summary):
- FIFO: best p50, worst p99 during spikes
- Soft-priority: isolates foreground at cost of background starvation
- EDF-preemptive: best p99 tradeoff, higher scheduler overhead and tiny request abort rate for very long KV states
- EDF-cohort: middle ground, lower implementation complexity than preemptive

Key observations / hypotheses:
- Preemption helps reduce p99 materially by allowing short-deadline short requests to skip long jobs currently executing on GPU. The KV-cache checkpoint/restore cost is the main limiter for how often preemption can be used.
- For models with long-kv states (>=4k tokens) the rollback/restore cost becomes non-trivial and introduces rare aborts; we need a safer checkpointing strategy or limits on preemption eligibility (e.g., only preempt if remaining_kv < 2k).
- EDF-preemptive increases scheduler CPU cycles but lowers GPU tail utilization variance -> suggests better user latency but more orchestration cost.
- Background starvation in strict lane-based soft-priority is a real product risk for multi-tenant customers unless we enforce fairness knobs.

Microprofile notes (profiling snippets):
- Context switch hotspot: scheduler.c:enqueue_again (12% of scheduler CPU time)
- KV checkpoint hot path: kvstore/serialize_chunk (avg 6ms for 2k tokens)
- Preempt decision latency: median 0.9ms, 95th 3.2ms

Open questions / TODOs:
- Run EDF-preemptive with quantized 4-bit kernels on mixed GPU types (A100 + H100) — does checkpoint cost scale differently?
- Try bounded preemption policy: disallow preemption if remaining_kv > 2048 tokens. Measure the abort rate and p99 impact.
- Add a fairness circuit-breaker to soft-priority lanes (credits per tenant) and replay the same workload to measure background SLA violation rate.
- Re-run long-run stability test (24h) to check memory fragmentation effects due to frequent checkpoint/restore.
- Add telemetry tags on requests that get preempted to trace user-visible errors and associate with customer ids for risk analysis.

Notes to self:
- Share preliminary numbers with Mira and Arjun; ask infra to spin a H100 node set for bounded test (JIRA-INF-1183).
- Keep preemption flag behind experiment gating and add server-side kill switch.

References and links: CONFLUENCE-3492 for design notes, JIRA-INF-1183 for infra requests, PR referenced above for tsurge changes (adds deadlines).

One-line summary to paste into standup: "EDF preemption reduces p99 by ~3x under synthetic spikes, but introduces a small abort rate for large KV sessions and ~8% scheduler CPU overhead — next: bounded-preempt policy + H100 runs."

End of scratchpad.
